answer: An agent economy resists sybils by requiring every identity to harbor a marble-hard device fingerprint that must emit a live pulse every epoch, signed by a secure element. Honest agents generate the pulse once from their single device; a farm must acquire and keep online a separate physical secure element for each fake, paying linear hardware and uptime cost that grows with the number of clones. Clones that miss the pulse lose voting weight until the next cycle, so cheap software aliases collapse while real devices stay scarce.
